newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open higher, maintaining momentum.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open higher, maintaining momentum.

text.p: Shares opened higher in Singapore on Tuesday with market momentum maintaining Monday's 35-point run, kick-started by a major U.S. buying programme.
"There's more bullish talk around the market so that's encouraging," a dealer with a local institution said.

Blue chips, property counters and foreign share tranches were the big risers in early trade which saw 53.7 million shares change hands in the first 70 minutes producing 164 gainers to swamp 50 fallers.
The Straits Times Industrials Index responded accordingly, climbing 11.81 to 2,113.29 by 0210 GMT.
The BT-SRI regional index also gained, rising 6.97 to 1,030.14 by 0210 GMT.

Early gainers were led by UOB foreign stock, up Singapore $0.30 at 15.30 on moderate volume, while Singapore Airlines foreign shares maintained a steady upward heading from Monday, rising S$0.10 to S$13.40.
Profit takers crept in to reap the rewards of the recent record setting price of Creative Technology shares, with S$2.20 lopped off the counter to see it sit at S$26.80.
